This relatively short incubation period is typical of many suboscine passerines in the Thamnophilidae family. The downy chicks are entirely dependent on bi-parental provisioning during the first days following hatching, as their eyes remain closed and their thermoregulatory capabilities are poorly developed. Parental feeding commences almost immediately after the trophic switch, with both adults contributing food items captured from the understory.
